title: Testing the search and checking answers

steps.say: The search of an application can be tested without the language model.
Each test question lists the reports expected among its passages.
This test passes because the expected report is among the four passages found.
The test set holds eight questions, each with its expected report.
Without a filter on the edition date, four of the eight tests pass. In the failed tests, passages from older editions take the place of the newest report.
With the filter, all eight tests pass. The tests make no call to the model and can run again after each change to the search.
In the chatbot, each figure of the answer carries a citation to a report and a page.
The citation of the poverty figure leads to page 23 of the June 2026 edition.
steps.speak: The citation of the poverty figure leads to page twenty-three of the June twenty twenty-six edition.

steps.say: The answer notes that its passage does not name the poverty line.
The sentence begins on page 22, which names the USD 3.00-per-day line.
steps.speak: The sentence begins on page twenty-two, which names the three dollar per day line.

steps.say: The tests check that the search finds the expected reports.
The reader uses the cited page to judge whether a figure answers the question. The page shows the measure and the period of the figure.
